title: Enter Action with Boldness
summary: Boldness and confidence are essential for power, while timidity and hesitation invite doubt and expose weaknesses. Bold actions create credibility, command attention, and instil fear, which helps establish authority. Conversely, acting with hesitation or only halfway creates self-doubt and allows others time to find flaws in your plans.
example: A con artist successfully sold the Eiffel Tower to a scrapper by executing a massive and bold lie.
A Russian prince who took action with guards already supporting his side.
reversal: Timidity is only useful when faked as a deception to set up a bolder strike later.
Bold or exaggerated moves must be calculated against the audience, as a smart target might call your bluff.
